--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_last_nodes_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the last N nodes that were created. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_last_nodes_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the last N nodes that were created. title: >- [Graph.select_last_nodes_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select the last N nodes that were created. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select the last N nodes that were created. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23565-L23650){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_last_nodes_created( n, set_op="union", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select last nodes created](/assets/graphs/select-last-nodes-created.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Six nodes A to F with filled badges 1 to 6 giving the order in which they were created. select_last_nodes_created(2) selects the two most recent, E and F, drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Selects the `n` most recently created nodes. The graph keeps track of the order in which nodes were added (see `get_node_creation_order()`), and this method takes the tail of that order. Nodes that have since been deleted are skipped, so the selection always refers to nodes that still exist. This is handy in incremental, build-as-you-go workflows, for example to: - tag or style the nodes that a generator such as `add_path_graph()` or `add_star_graph()` just added, with `set_node_attrs_ws()` - connect a freshly added batch of nodes to each other with `fully_connect_nodes_ws()` - undo the last few additions with `delete_nodes_ws()` Selection is based on creation order, not on node IDs or labels. The nodes are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of most recently created nodes to select. Must be a non-negative integer (a negative value raises `OverflowError`). If `n` is larger than the number of nodes, every node is selected; `n=0` selects nothing. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How these nodes combine with the current node selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected nodes among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selection follows creation order rather than label order, so this selects whichever two nodes were added most recently -- here "C" and "D": ::: {#63d1b638 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .select_last_nodes_created(2) ) selected = graph.get_selected_node_ids() sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in selected) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['C', 'D'] ``` ::: ::: A typical use is labelling the output of a generator. After adding a 3-node path to an existing node "root", the last three nodes are exactly the ones the generator created, so only they get `batch=2`: ::: {#21a1bd59 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="root", batch=1) .add_path_graph(3) .select_last_nodes_created(3) .set_node_attrs_ws(batch=2) ) graph.get_node_df().select("id", "label", "batch") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
